utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, The Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj. The.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. So this is Wednesday, the 2nd of April, 2008, and I welcome the members of the OTP, Mr. Mundis, Ms. Biersay, our witness, as well as Mr. Seselj and all the others helping us. We are going to continue the cross-examination. Mr. Seselj has one hour and 39 minutes left, and, Mr. Seselj, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, first of all I have to bring two matters to your attention of a procedural nature. First, yesterday, the Registrar, without authorisation, censored the entire proceedings, and through the internet all that you could see was 30 to 40 minutes of these proceedings. All the rest was represented as having been conducted in closed session. And the television broadcast yesterday, or rather last night, there was just 30 to 40 minutes of these proceedings shown. Now, from the beginning of the second session, when the Prosecutor asked to go into closed session, and then right up until the end, everything was closed session, even the half hour of my cross-examination, although everything must have been in open session. So I demand that you instruct the Registrar to find a way of rectifying this and broadcasting it via the internet, because of all principles of these proceedings, the public nature of the trial is the most important one as far as I'm concerned. And then there is a problem in the detention centre, in prison, which for the next 20 days to one month will make it more difficult for my trial, because there is some construction work going on, so they're moving us around from one floor to another, and I'm not going to have the necessary time and conditions to set out my documents, and everything will have to be packed into boxes. So I demand that you instruct the Prosecutor tomorrow and, at the latest, the day after, a firm schedule for April so that I can set aside all the documents that I will need for April to be able to prepare my defence successfully, because if my documents are packed up, as of next week, I'm not going to have any quality time to prepare for the proceedings. So those are the two matters which I wish to raise this morning of a procedural nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The first issue, the internet broadcast. Why is it that only 30 minutes out of some four hours of hearing were to be broadcast? I don't know. The Registrar and the Legal Officer are going to look into this, and the Trial Chamber will keep you abreast of developments. The second thing, the construction work underway in the jail. This is news to me. Of course, this might have consequences or an impact on how you can prepare for your defence. We will talk to the prison manager so he can tell us how he can make sure not to disturb you, to disturb you as least as possible. And regarding the list of witnesses for April, I think we already had a draft list. Maybe Mr. Mundis could send it to you quickly without any problems. Mr. Mundis, regarding April witnesses for the four weeks to come, do you have a list?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We'll provide that list later this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you will have this list at the end of the day, at least. We are in open session. At 9.31, I will check that everything is being broadcast on the internet, of course, if there's no closed session in between. Now you have the floor again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. VS-033, you gave two statements to The Hague Tribunal, one in 2004 and another one in 2006; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In neither of these two statements did you mention this alleged killing of the volunteer Muslim by the other volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party, did you? You mentioned that for the first time on the 26th of July and 28th of March this year, at the proofing session with the investigator, Paolo Pastorre-Stocchi; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So this very notable thing, if it were true, you just seemed to forget to say in 2004 and 2006; it was only subsequently that you thought up telling this lie about an event that never happened; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: No, that isn't right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. If it's not right, I have proof to show that it was. You can say whatever you like. Now, in addition to the fact that you told a lie about Goran Hadzic receiving the first group of volunteers, you subsequently, in the proofing session, said that he was also -- they were also welcomed by Veljko Dzakula, although you never mentioned Dzakula's name either in 2004 or 2006; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: I didn't know at the time what his name was. I forgot his surname. But after talking to some volunteers, I remembered later on what his surname was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you didn't know how to differentiate between Eastern and Western Slavonia, so you inserted Goran Hadzic there, although he never had any institutional authority there; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether he had any power and authority, but he was there and greeted us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In your first statement, in paragraph 22, you state that -- in your first statement, you said that the Serbian Radical Party -- no, it's not paragraph 22. Anyway, you said that the Serbian Radical Party, for every volunteer, received 1.000 German marks from the Territorial Defence of Western Slavonia and the DB of Serbia; is that right? Did you say that, in fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: That's what I heard up at the front, at the battlefield, from the commander of the village in Western Slavonia, and I stated that, yes. Q.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. One, I'm finding it very difficult to hear the translation in my headphones because of the voice of Mr. Seselj is reaching this far. And, secondly, I do have the statements of the witness in his language, if it would be of assistance to him.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no need, because the witness remembers it all, and that's what the witness said in paragraph 22 of his statement of 2006. And in the statement of 2004, he makes no mention of that at all. So those are the facts, and don't take up my time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you told a lie about that, too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: No, I did not tell a lie. I mentioned it. Perhaps the Prosecution failed to record it, but I'm sure I mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Then you go on to say that General Anton Tus gave you a certificate or authorisation for fuel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Radovan and I interpreted the signature as "Tus," but Radovan went to the headquarters because not everybody can receive this authorisation for fuel. It has to be an authorised officer. You can't have an ordinary soldier issuing authorisation of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You even quote the words, allegedly, of General Tus; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Radovan told me that the officer who gave him the authorisation told him that he would best like to arrest us, but he couldn't do that because he had an order from the leadership that he had to assist us and had to give it to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you drew the conclusion that that was Anton Tus who, in November of 1991, wasn't in the JNA at all then; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: At that time, he was in the JNA, and then he left some ten days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is he was not in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: All right, well, I don't know that. But, anyway -- well, I don't know that. All I do know is what Radovan and I discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you must absolutely turn off your microphone, because this witness is granted protective measures. And, please, make a break between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: General Anton Tus was the commander of the Air Force and Anti-Air Defence, and he was pensioned off from that post sometime in June 1995, and several months later he went to Croatia. Now, when you were lying and were saying that he gave you this authorisation, you had absolutely no idea who he was or what he was. You heard the name "Anton Tus," the signature seemed to be something like "Tos," and so why not, you can sell that to The Hague Tribunal because they don't have any idea about anything, anyway. Furthermore, you stated, and that was in paragraph 33 of the statement of 2006, that with the volunteers in Western Slavonia, there was an official of the State Security, and that you concluded that he submitted reports and that Ljubisa Petkovic was frequently in contact with officials from the DP, et cetera. In 2004 you make no mention of that whatsoever. And you also told the lie with respect to any DB official with the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party in Western Slavonia; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. Now, you also told another lie and said that I wanted to kill Radovan Novacic and that Novacic wanted to kill me. Now, I have here a statement from Radovan Novacic, where he refutes both lies. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: No, it's not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You also lied in paragraph 56. You said: "When I attended a dinner in Zvecevo, organised by Colonel Trbojevic," where you were not, but the entire leadership of Western Slovenia did attend the dinner, including Veljko Dzakula, Veljko Vukelic, and Ilija Sasic, and so on and so forth, and you said that Trbojevic then gave me a brown bag with some money. You slipped that into your statement of 2006, whereas you don't say that in the 2004 statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: What I said is correct, and I did attend a dinner. I didn't take part. I was the security detail for you, because Radovan Novacic put up the volunteers in the Zvecevo Hotel to provide security while you were there. So you stayed for a brief period of time. You didn't even have dinner. You just had a little something to eat, and you picked up your brief case. One was brown, the other was blue. I don't know about the blue one, what was in there, but I do know there was money in the brown brief case, because I was standing to your left just two metres away and I saw you open the brief case and saw that the money was inside and Zoran Miscevic brought it to you. He handed it over to you personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So now I have two brief case, one brown and one blue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you say Zoran Miscevic gave me the money and I opened it and counted the money?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: You didn't count it. He said, "Do you want to count it?" You said, "There was no need." You just took a glance and said, "There was no need for the money to be counted."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All that's a lie. That's all lies, and you didn't remember to mention that here yesterday, either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Mr. Seselj, I've been told that after you ask your question, please turn off your microphone. If you don't turn off your microphone, then the answer of the witness can be heard through your own microphone, without distortion, and that is a technical problem that has just been brought to my attention. Mrs. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: The problem is also compounded by the volume of Mr. Seselj's voice, so if he could just speak a little bit lower, then I could actually hear the translation and maybe it wouldn't travel into the witness's microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj will do his utmost to make sure we don't run into technical problems. Now, Witness, please, I would like to come back to an issue that might be minor or major. I don't know yet how it will turn out. In your written statement, you said -- and Mr. Seselj asked you questions about this. So you said that Mr. Seselj allegedly intended to have Novacic killed, and I thought I understood that Novacic seemed to have the same plan, which is quite surprising. Why would Mr. Seselj want Mr. Novacic killed? Do you have an explanation for this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The explanation is because Novacic already had problems in the territory of Western Slavonia, and people had already been sent from the Radical Party who did want to kill him at the headquarters at Lager, so that when we were down there at the War Staff, we heard that they were waiting for him all up there to kill him, up at the headquarters there. And Novacic gathered together his men, and I was one of them, and we went to the War Staff to see who it was who wanted to kill him. However, Mr. Seselj, with his security guards, had left, and the people up there -- Slavko Misic was there and some more volunteers, quite a number of them, and Ljubisa Petkovic was up there, and he managed to calm the situation down at the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So it seems that there was a plan to kill Novacic, but what was the motivation behind it? Why did people want Novacic killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know why they wanted to kill him. All I can do is assume -- well, since in the War Staff, when they wanted to kill him at Lager, it was, "Don't call Radovan, call Goran." And as I was with him all the time, and I know what from what he said, that they used to refer to him as "Goran" when he was small, but he was actually named "Radovan" by the best man, they wanted to use that, that this was a man who had been infiltrated from Croatia and that he was a spy and that they should kill him at Lager. And since some people from Belgrade knew me, some of the volunteers from Belgrade, they listened to me, and I explained to them that -- what the situation was like and what Radovan's situation was like, that he was called "Goran" when he was a small child, but that in fact he was Radovan. Everybody in his family called him "Goran." But they wanted to use this mix-up and say he was a Croatian spy. This was at Lager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So if I understood you well, there was a suspicion that he might be a Croat spy infiltrated within the SRS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But if that was true, he should have been killed later on, which never happened. Why is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, because he didn't go back to Lager. Had he gone back to Western Slavonia, they probably would have killed him, but he went to Loznica, and by doing that he managed saved his life. Otherwise, they would have killed him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, please resume.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And since that killing was quite obviously, in your opinion, a way in which I behaved, do you know of any instance where I killed someone or that somebody was killed pursuant to my orders? Tell me that, then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, the volunteers at the battle front certainly didn't go to pick any corn.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, what did they do pursuant to my orders? Did the volunteers kill the maise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, they didn't pick it, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, the volunteers went to war to fight, and when somebody is killed on the battleground, it's not murder as a criminal act. I'm asking you: Do you know -- can you quote a single instance where I killed a man, and give me his name and surname, or that anybody following orders from me specifically killed someone? Not to go into battle and kill someone in battle during the fighting, but that he expressly killed an individual pursuant to my orders. Quote me anything like that, if you can.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: I don't know about any killings, but I know about people being beaten up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And who was beaten up on my orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] [French spoken]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again a problem with the mic, Mr. Seselj, a technical problem. It should work now. Witness, you partially answered the question. You said that you know of somebody who was beaten. Who, when, and how, and where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I was in the Serbian volunteers fund, the office was shared with the SCP, so I know about some people who, on the orders of Drazilovic, went and beat people up who were not -- he did not share their political opinions. But that was when a group left the Radical Party, and then they were mistreated and beaten up. These were the volunteers from Palilula.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: One name, please give us one name of a man who left the Serbian Radical Party and that then Drazilovic gave the order for him to be beaten up. Who was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, at that time Jovic, this guy Jovic, and I know that -- well, I can't really attribute that to you, but his wife, Pa ska, had her throat slit at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: First of all, Slobodan Jovic's wife was killed several years after he left the Serbian Radical Party, is that right, and she was killed in the course of a robbery of a store that she owned. And now you want to say that this was done on my orders; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, at that time you were at the CZ, at the time when she was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And from the prison, I gave an order for Slobodan Jovic's wife to be killed? I had already forgotten all about him .

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: I'm not saying that you issued the order for her to be killed, but pressure was exerted on those people who left the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's remark: Could the witness and Mr. Seselj please not speak at the same time. It's impossible to interpret.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you're not able to give us a single name of a member of the Serbian Radical Party who was beaten up by the activists of the party. In 2004, you stated that I and the Serbian State Security Service, and the Unit for Special Operations, the so-called Red Berets, organised the transportation by helicopter of Serb volunteers to Srebrenica, and that from the volunteers who had been in Srebrenica, you heard that the volunteers there were under the control of the Red Berets and that they wore red berets themselves. That was in 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then when you gave a new statement in 2006, you left that out. There is no mention of it at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, I didn't leave that out. Perhaps it's the OTP that left it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The OTP left it out because even the OTP could not buy the lie of this proportions, because the Prosecution knows that in July 1995, when the operation to liberate Srebrenica was underway, I was incarcerated by Milosevic, and that's something that you did not have in mind; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I object to this line of -- it's not even questioning, but testimony and commentary by Mr. Seselj. To the extent that he has a question for the witness, he should pose it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Seselj, please ask your questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I keep asking my questions, and I mention things, incredible things, from the statements that the witness made that he did not mention in his examination-in-chief, and I'm trying to show that between 2004 and 2006, the OTP got scared because of the magnitude of the lies this witness furnished to them and that that cannot be based on anything. I was incarcerated for two months in the prison in Gnjilane, and to say that I organised my volunteers to go to Srebrenica at that time, with Milosevic's forces -- this witness is incredibly important for me. He is the very image of the OTP, in moral sense and in every other sense, because you can see from the testimony of this witness in which way the OTP is operating and how deep embroiled in all these lies it is. Unfortunately, this worked fine for them in many of the cases before this Tribunal. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You say that volunteers said to you that volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party went to Srebrenica with a unit of the Red Berets. And you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in Skelani and in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the accused said earlier on that at that time he was in prison. Does that seem possible to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, he's not the only one in command of the Radical Party and the volunteers. Well, the party continues to function even though he's in prison now, regardless of where he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But in the Gnjilane prison, I was together with Tomislav Nikolic and a large number of other officials from the Serbian Radical Party. Almost the entire leadership was arrested by Milosevic, and the rest of the activists and leaders cooperated with Milosevic and sent volunteers to Srebrenica. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: No, that's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was Tomislav Nikolic with me in the prison in Gnjilane?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, I don't know who was with you in prison, but I do know that the volunteers went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then again you lied, that I had ordered that the Muslim -- that the Muslims be attacked with automatic rifles at the Belgrade mosque as they left their prayers at 6.00 p.m. That's what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: I said that your man from your security, Vojkan Pacov, a major, that was his nickname, that he ordered us to do that and that we chased him away from the party because nobody liked him, and that's why we forced him out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How did you force him out of the party when you were not a member of the Serbian Radical Party at the time? You left the Serbian Radical Party in early 1992, and you joined the White Eagles.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And in 1992, you were at Vojkovic with the White Eagles. That's what you say in your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: No, I did not join the White Eagles, that's not correct, and I was at the Serbian Volunteers Fund which was at the SCP. The SCP and the humanitarian organisation, the Serbian Volunteers, shared the same office.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How is it that you were not in the White Eagles when, in your statement here, you say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I think Mr. Seselj anticipated my objection. Could he please direct us to the paragraphs to which he's referring when he poses these questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The reference to the White Eagles, where did he say that, Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's at paragraph 64 of the 2004 statement, and then another mention is made in paragraph 63 of the 2006 statement. But in paragraph 64, the 2004 one, he says that in late 1992 or 1993, through Goran Stojkovic and the Serbian National Defence, that Dragoslav Bokan contacted him and asked him to train his men at Vojkovici in Republika Srpska near Sarajevo for 15 days of his absence, and so on and so forth, and he goes on to describe all that, and he says that they were all promised a thousand German marks and so on. Now, in the 2006 statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to explain first of all, she can't really be interrupting every sentence that I start, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with you, but if Ms. Biersay gets up, stands up, she thinks that there is something important. What is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, instead of Mr. Seselj representing to the witness what the witness said, I believe it would be helpful for the witness to actually look at the statements that he provided.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm moving on. I don't have time to waste. You're simply trying to find methods to make me waste as much time as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: VS-033, you should have read those statements before you appeared in court. I have another question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Can I answer the previous question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Dragoslav Bokan asked me to look after his people at Vojkovic village and for us conduct some kind of training before he manages to gather all his people in Vojkovici, and he said that he would be there. We went there as mercenaries. He said that everybody -- every man would receive 1.000 German marks per month. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. VS-033, when was the first time that you got in touch with Natasha Kandic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. The Serbian authority didn't want to issue an ID to me for four and a half months, and I had to go and talk to somebody, because I wanted to come here and testify. I couldn't get the ID card for four and a half months, and usually you get it immediately. Even the worst criminals get it immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What year did it happen? When did you talk to Natasha Kandic to get her to do something about your ID card?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Last year.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And before that, did you have any contact with her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: No, never before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you be so kind as to show the witness document number nine. It's a statement by a Defence witness, Aleksandar Gajic, and this witness knows this man quite well, and he will tell us everything about the context of this witness and Natasha Kandic. I received this yesterday by fax.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. In quickly looking at this, not that I read Cyrillic -- excuse me, this one isn't in Cyrillic. But to the extent that it gives the name -- gives us the true name of the witness, I would ask that we move to private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I propose that the screen be shown only for us in court, and as we quote parts of this document, I will not be mentioning the name of this witness. I will just mention the name of Aleksandar Gajic and not Natasha Kandic. Aleksandar Gajic is my Defence witness and Natasha Kandic must be mentioned here, so I would like us not to go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in technical terms, there is this possibility for not broadcasting this document outside, so we can go ahead in this manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you have this document in front of you now? Is it on the screen? This is a statement made by Aleksandar Gajic on the 31st of March, 2008, and it was certified by the competent court in Belgrade. You can see that here, in the first paragraph, he talks about what he knows about the methods used by the OTP in The Hague, false accusations, and about his reasons why he got in touch with my expert team assisting me with my defence. And here he starts to discuss Natasha Kandic and you, and let us move on to the next paragraph and I will read this paragraph to you. He says: "In the summer of 2007, I," and then he mentions your name, "was called" -- I will speak slowly: "I was called on the phone, and he told me that he had gotten in touch with Natasha Kandic from the Humanitarian Law Centre in Belgrade, and that he had been there several times to receive instructions and to be proofed in the premises of the Humanitarian Rights Centre at McKenzie Street and that he had agreed to testify as a Prosecution witness at the Tribunal in The Hague at the trial against Professor Vojislav Seselj and that Natasha Kandic wanted to get her revenge on the Serbian Radical Party and Professor Vojislav Seselj because she pathologically hated Vojislav Seselj." Did you, in the summer of 2007, call Aleksandar Gajic and tell him that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: This is not true at all. Aleksandar Gajic introduced me to Natasha Kandic, in fact. This is definitely not correct, and I am not surprised that you received such statements from Serbia, because mafia rules in Serbia and you are part of the mafia, and it's not the state that is in power. Everything -- all the institutions, the judicial system is contaminated, so I'm not surprised. God knows what kind of pressure this man was under when he was forced to write something like that. I wouldn't like to be in his skin, seeing what he had to write. I know this man. He's one of my best friends, and I'm really sorry -- I feel really sorry for him. God knows what you're doing to him in Serbia; not only to him, but to all the others, when they have to write these kind of lies. I went to elementary school with him, and I know him, I know this man.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And when was the last time that you were in contact with Aleksandar Gajic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, I can't recall now. Two months ago, a month ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, you're lying again, Mr. VS-033. You called him last night twice and you sent him an SMS message, using your phone here in The Hague, (redacted).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, if you give his phone number, everybody will know who he is, so we'll have to redact this.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could we go into private session briefly, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let's go into private session, because we're talking here about personal issues with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall have a 20-minute break now. Yes, I thought we'd begun at half past 8.00, but we began at 9.00, so we still have 30 minutes ahead of us. My mistake. I thought we had begun earlier today. Mr. Seselj, you have 30 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean 30 minutes to the break? I hope not 30 minutes in total.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have 30 minutes until the break. So far, you've used up 56 minutes. You have one hour and four minutes left.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let's start off with the last paragraph now, which is particularly interesting to me because it speaks about the methodology employed by Natasha Kandic in her work and Natasha Kandic appears with every false witness. So, Mr. VS-033, I'm now going to read out that particular paragraph. Aleksandar Gajic writes as follows: "In my intention to learn whether it was true, at the proposal," and then he mentions your name, "I went with him to a meeting with Natasha Kandic, to her flat, which is located in Gvozdiceva [phoen] Street in Belgrade, not far from the St. Sava Church." Now, next page, please: "I was directly taken there," and then he says your name, "on that occasion," and then once again your name, "introduced me to Natasha Kandic as a potential Prosecution witness against Vojislav Seselj, which took me by surprise. I noticed that Natasha Kandic at that point in time was very pleased, and she said, 'Now I have another witness against Vojislav Seselj,' adding that rarely did people dare to testify against Vojislav Seselj. "Now, to uncover the real intentions of Natasha Kandic, I agreed to cooperate with her in order to be able to arrive at information about her hostile activity and activity against the Serb people, the Serb Radical Party, and Professor Dr. Vojislav Seselj." She was convinced that she had found a true and real collaborator and cooperator. Natasha Kandic gave me her telephone numbers, her landline, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. We will redact everything dealing with the address and the telephone number of Natasha Kandic. Continue, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since you've redacted that, we can move on to the next paragraph straight away, because he mentions her mobile telephone number. So it's not anything that's terribly secret, in my opinion, but never mind. We can see that he knows all the numbers and he knows Natasha Kandic's address, where she resides, and then Aleksandar Gajic goes on to state the following: "As the trial against Professor Vojislav Seselj has started, I keep getting telephone calls from Natasha Kandic inviting me, together with," and then she says your name, it almost slipped out, I've just remembered, anyway, "to go to the premises for the Fund for Humanitarian Law on an unspecified day in the summer of 2007," and you, your name, "came to so me, and he insisted that I ring up Natasha Kandic and ask her whether she is free and whether she wishes to receive us for talks. I rang up Natasha Kandic over the phone, and she told me -- told us to take a taxi to take us to the Fund for Humanitarian Law and that she would pay for the taxi." And then she mentions your name again and says: "He and I went to Natasha Kandic together on the premises of the Fund for Humanitarian Law, where she greeted us." And then he goes on to say that they came across some women there, they introduced themselves as victims from Srebrenica, and things like that. So we can skip over the next part. Anyway, Aleksandar Gajic goes on to say lower down the following: "Before we set off to see Natasha Kandic," and then mentions your name, "told me that he was going to stack up things for the Serbian Radical Party and Professor Dr. Vojislav Seselj and Ljubisa Petkovic, to the effect that they had committed crimes in Western Slavonia and other places in Croatia and Bosnia. And when I asked him, 'Man, how can you fabricate such lies and accuse other people of crimes they did not commit,'" and then they mentioned your name, "told me," and there are some swear words here which I don't want to repeat, but you invoke my mother in those swear words, et cetera, "and then Aleksandar Gajic" -- do you want me to read it out or do you want it to read out? Or shall we skip over those swear words? What do you think, VS-033, shall we skip them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Skip them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: No probative value at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we don't know if there's any probative value, whether there's relevance as to the credibility of the witness, so the question could be raised. But there's another problem here, Mr. Seselj. On screen now we have a text that does not seem to correspond with the document number 9, page 17, 18, 19 and 20. Is this a mistake or not?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this ought to be page 18 now, but we can't see the whole page on the screen. I don't think it's a mistake. But, anyway, I skipped that portion, I didn't read the whole of that paragraph out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can resume.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the lady can shift the page so we can see the very bottom of the page, because that's where I'd like to read from now, that's where I got to. We can see the end part now, and I'm going to read the sentence out. Where your name was mentioned, Aleksandar Gajic mentions your name, Witness, and said you told him that Natasha Kandic had promised him a lot of money just to Vojislav Seselj and his volunteers. Now, did Natasha indeed promise you any remuneration, Mr. VS-033?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: That's a blatant lie. And it says here he called Natasha Kandic. Now, why would he call up Natasha Kandic if allegedly I was a friend of hers, as you said at the beginning?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, that's not strange.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Why would I tell him to call if I was supposed to call, if I want to call someone, I call that person up. I'm not going to say, "Now, you call the person up and agree on a meeting." I would do that myself, if I wanted to, which means that you can see that he's lying here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, that's nothing strange, because you came to his flat and you told him to call up Natasha Kandic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, we're friends from childhood, he and I.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This time, the witness is interrupting me. So you went to see him, to his home, and told him to call her up, and I suppose you're both friends with Natasha Kandic, so why shouldn't he ring her up and the telephone was in his apartment, so there's nothing strange about that; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: No, it's not. I was a friends with him since childhood, so if I go to his house, I can ring up and use his phone myself. There's no need for him to do that. If I want to insist on something, then I can pick up the phone and call.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Okay, let us move on, let's move on to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: This is exactly why perhaps we need to be in private session, if Mr. Seselj is unable to respect the protective measures of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did I mention the name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I did, then I apologise. It can be redacted. It happened by accident, it can be redacted from the recording, and I don't think it's a problem for it to be redacted both from the transcript and the recording.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will skip one section again, and let me move on to the last paragraph on this page, although I marked the whole statement as important, but I don't have time to show you everything. But you can take a copy of it with you. I don't have anything against that. Aleksandar Gajic goes on to say: "In early January 2008, I went to the apartment of," mentioning your name, in the street that's the address, where -- and it says who lives there with you, and he says that you called Natasha Ka ndic on the phone, and then I go on to quote: "And in my presence, he asked her to give him safe passage from Belgrade to (redacted) so that he can stay there and prepare for the trial as a Prosecution witness against Vojislav Seselj." Did you really spend the first months of this year in (redacted) preparing for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: This is nothing but a lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I really would like to hear what the Prosecution wants to say. Are they objecting because this is not true or because of protective measures?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Biersay, what are the grounds for your objection? What are you objecting to?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I am objecting to Mr. Seselj using information that is highly likely to identify this witness, specifically, which includes various locations connected to this witness, which includes the association between Mr. Gajic and this witness and the nature of their relationship. And we do believe that this tends to identify, specifically, this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you heard the witness say that it is (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The lie is that Natasha Kandic organised that. That's the lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But so you did go there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. (redacted) (redacted), I believe that the Trial Chamber should consult on this first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Trial Chamber

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: Resume, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I will not mention this section that has been redacted. Let us move on to page 4. I don't have much time. I would like to finish this topic by the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Here, you can see that on several occasions over the past two months, you used your mobile phone to send messages to Aleksandar Gajic once you heard that he would appear as a Defence witness. So it was not only last night that you were in contact with him. Over the past two months, you were in contact with him on several occasions, yet you claim that you were not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Had I known that he was a Defence witness earlier, I would not have contacted him at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you'd never heard my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, let me answer this one first, because you always ask ten questions, but let me answer now. Had I known, but I didn't know --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But please wait for my question. I know that you are nervous. You have every reason to be nervous. You were caught in a lie. The Trial Chamber is now aware of the fact that you are a big liar, because you face criminal prosecution because of the lies. You lied under oath and you lied before the Trial Chamber that you didn't send any SMS messages --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, nobody mentioned any SMS messages. I was talking about whether I talked to him or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, very well. Mr. Seselj and Mr. Witness, please, do not speak so loudly. Your voice is so loud now that no one can be heard, so make sure that one asks the question, the other one answers the question. Mr. Seselj, ask your question.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note, the witness and Mr. Seselj are speaking at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Since I don't want to go into closed session again, you have several SMS messages here, three of them, the ones that you sent at an earlier time to Aleksandar Gajic, and he noted them down. Do you confirm that these are the three messages that you sent, that you're threatening him with Paolo, whatever his name is, Stocchi? I filed a criminal report against him recently. Did you send these three messages to Aleksandar Gajic; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, please. It seems that the interpreters into French noted something which I believe is important. I would like her to be able to repeat it, and I would like it to also to be translated into English. I think it's really important to be able to understand the question of the contacts.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Judge, would you like me to read out those three messages?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that's not the problem. Mr. Seselj, at one point in time you talked about the contacts, and it seems that in your own language there are two words that may have two meanings. The interpreter into French, who knows your language, will tell us what are these two versions, and this will also be translated into English. So could the interpreter in the B/C/S-French booth tell us, what are the two meanings of "contact" in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. President, it's probably the best -- the best thing to do would be for me to explain, because you don't have a better expert for Serbian language than I am. "Contact" means every contact, a meeting, a telephone --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, the interpreter is talking. It's an official interpreter from this Tribunal. You are not the official interpreter of this Tribunal. You're not even a witness. So please let the interpreter speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the interpreter say, in Serbian, what these two words are? And Mr. Seselj will comment if he wishes to. Please repeat what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Listening to someone, and the other is "kontaktirati," meaning having contact with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the second one is "kontaktirati," and my Serbian is not very good, to say the least, but those are the two words. Mr. Seselj, any comment on this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never used the word "cuti se," to talk to someone, because if somebody -- if we use this word, it means to talk to somebody on the phone. I said "contact," and the word "contact," uses -- talking to somebody, letters, meeting somebody, messages, any kind of contact, I was specific here, and the witness denied everything.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, sending an SMS message, that is a direct thing, and contacting somebody is to talk to somebody, "cuti se," over the phone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now you have a witness who is an expert in the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the way I understood it, "cuti se," "kontaktirati," that means to talk to somebody.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are a few minutes before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In the next paragraph after the three messages --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: May I comment on those messages?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Please wait for me to ask you a question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, but what question am I supposed to answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In the next paragraph, Aleksandar Gajic says that on the 14th of March, 2008, because he's noting down every contact with him very diligently, at 1948 hours, from the phone he notes the number that you called him, and that you were intoxicated, and that you said -- and then he goes on to quote you, that you had called a man. I don't want to mention his name, because that man should not know that you are here in the courtroom. That you cursed him, cursing his mother, and that you said that you would kill Aleksandar Vucic, Tomo Nikolic, and that you were -- you would send from that location where you had been in hiding with the assistance of Natasha Kandic, some people to get rid of him. This is what Aleksandar Gajic noted down, and I want to know if this is true or not. I don't want to hear your comments, why you did that, but is it true that there was this telephone conversation and that this is what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: There was this telephone conversation, because my family received threats, and I said that if anything happened to my family, that I would have my revenge. So, yes, there was this contact with Gajic, but I don't know the exact date. It was -- what's the date here, the 14th of March? Yes, it may have been the 14th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Gajic --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: But I guess this was in February. I don't think that it was really on the 14th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Gajic, from this --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: And I did not curse anyone's mother, and I did not mention in that conversation Tomo Nikolic. I did mention the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you threatened only Vucic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: I did not threaten anyone. I merely said -- I did not make any threats. I said -- I just said that they should be careful about what they are doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Okay, if that's not a threat, then we can go on. As this text goes on, Aleksandar Gajic says: "I had the opportunity to see and to make sure that this man," and your name is mentioned, "that he spends a lot of money in restaurants every day, that he drives -- he goes around in taxis every day and he smokes expensive cigarettes, yet he does not have a job, and he spends lots of money. I was able to see that this started when he got in contact with Natasha Kandic and when he started cooperating with her. On one occasion, he showed me a large number of Euros saying, 'Atso [phoen], you're crazy,' agreed cooperate with Natasha Kandic and with the Tribunal in The Hague, 'We will live like emperors, we will have as much money as we need. We can go to and live in some other country. The Tribunal in The Hague will pay for all that. Come on, brother, let's do'" something "'to Seselj.'" It was actually a swear word, and I am such a polite man I don't want to repeat the swear word that you used: "Let us go to some other country and let's get some black women to wave around, to cool us off, and we will just drink and make merry on the beach." So it seems that you think that black women are predestined for that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, I can't imagine that Aleksandar Gajic would say that. Is he alive at all? I don't know what you did to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He will appear in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note, it is impossible to interpret when the witness and Mr. Seselj are speaking at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj. Well, Mr. Seselj, put your question, wait for the answer -- and wait for the answer to be over before you ask a new question. You are talking at the same time as the witness, and the witness also is not waiting for the end of your question to answer. It's 10.30, and the Registrar has told me that for technical reasons we need a 30-minute break, so I think this will help us cool down, and we'll meet again at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are back in session. Let me ask Madam Registrar to go into private session. We are going to speak to Mr. Seselj right now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I first have to make an objection or to tell you something, Judge. I spoke to my assistants, who are at my disposal at all times, and they are watching what is being broadcast over the internet, and they realised that the Registry censored the first session again. The moment I started pulling out of those documents out of my pocket, they went into closed session. And you know that we were not in closed session at that time. They censored much more of the material than the Court decided. And you can check that. You can see that the moment I pull out those papers out of my pocket, we move into closed session without your decision. I will continue with my questions for this Prosecution -- for this protected witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. VS-33, when Natasha Kandic introduced you to journalist Dana Tanasijevic from the Vreme newspaper, when was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: With Natasha Kandic and Dana Tanasijevic you arranged that you would put a hand grenade on your windowsill and that you would tie the safety pin to the window itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, this is pure fabrication. I really don't know how I could respond to such lies. This makes no sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then Dana Tanasijevic had a press conference where he made an accusation that through my wife, Jadranka Seselj, I sent a message to some criminals that they should do that on my behalf; that was the setup.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, I cannot reply to something that is a pure lie. What you said is pure fabrication. This is fabrication.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And, Mr. VS-033, when did you throw a makeshift explosive device on the Belgrade mosque, since you are an expert for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was it in December?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Yes, December, thereabouts. I don't know the exact month, whether it was in December, but it was in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the police managed to identify you in 1996; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please be so kind and put document number 11 on the ELMO for the witness, and it should not be broadcast for the public because it might lead to disclosing the identity of this witness, because his name is mentioned in this document. While we're waiting for this document to come up:

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You got training on how to handle explosives in the army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Here we have a decision from the Administration for the Suppression of Crime of the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia. We have the number and the date. The date is the 20th of April, 1996, and this decision indicates that you were to be remanded in custody because there were grounds for suspicion that you committed a crime qualified as unauthorised purchase and carrying of explosives and ammunition. The this is signed by an authorised official. We don't have to mention his name. But is this an authentic document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Yes, I think it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Okay. Let us now move on to document number 2. This is while they were still unaware of the fact that you threw this explosive device on the mosque. I'm sorry, that's number 12. At the time when you threw this bomb on the mosque, you were not a member of the Serbian Radical Party and you had nothing to do with the party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Yes, I had nothing to do with the party, but I was a member of the Humanitarian Fund of Serbian Volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I'm not interested in that. You may have established this fund or whatever?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I'm not interested in that because that has nothing to do with the Serbian Radical Party. This is a certificate for temporarily-seized items issued by the Secretariat of the Interior in Belgrade, that's the Belgrade Police Administration, the date is 19th of April, 1996, and it is indicated here what was found in your apartment when it was searched; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, we see 500 grams of plastic explosive, PEP 500, and we have also the designations, PIG 8603 in its original packaging; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then one package of explosive, 100 grams; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: 180 grams of black gunpowder, 3.53 metres of slow-burning fuse; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Four electric detonation fuses, is that right, eight detonation fuses; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Then 13 pieces of 7.62-calibre bullets for automatic rifle. We don't have to read it to the end, but this was all that was found and seized at your place. Is this an authentic document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now move on to document number 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, can I just ask you: These documents appear to have been issued in 1996, and I believe the witness said that the incident with the mosque took place in 1992, so in which way are these documents related to the throwing of the makeshift explosive device at the mosque in Belgrade in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Judge, you may have mis-heard this, but the witness confirmed that for three or four years, the police was unable to identify him as the perpetrator, as the man who threw this bomb at the Belgrade mosque. He was identified only in 1996. And you will see all this is made quite specific in the documents that will follow. I am working through this at this pace so that I would be able to present all of those documents in brief to you. So the witness also confirms that this has to do with this incident when bomb was thrown at the mosque. Can he confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this 1996 has nothing to do with the mosque. This is what I had in my home.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: It's not really an objection, it's just an observation, that Mr. Seselj is not turning off his mic before the witness responds.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the witness is lying once again. You will see that all this has to do with this bomb-throwing incident, first of all this decision to remand him in custody that I presented first, then the certificate. Once he was taken into custody, his apartment was searched. And now we have a request for an investigation to be conducted from the public prosecutor's office in Belgrade. We have the reference number, you can see it here. I don't want to identify the case. The date is the 24th of April, 1996. And here, in paragraph 2, we see the name of this witness, and we see his accomplices. We will not be mentioning them. And you can see here in this text that this is a crime qualified as endangering security and fomenting national -- ethnic and religious hatred. And this crime was committed in such a way that this man, with another man, fashioned a makeshift explosive device, using plastic explosive and fuses, that they wanted to activate and set in the mosque yard or underneath the windows of the apartments or underneath the cars owned by citizens of the FRY of Muslim faith or of Croatian ethnicity, and you can see who stood guard as they did that. It is also noted that explosions were caused that resulted in danger to the life of people and property, large-scale damage to properties.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then we have a description of what each of them did, and under number 1 it stipulates the name of this witness and his accomplices, and it says that on the 8th of December, 1992, at around 1830 hours, in Belgrade, Gospodar Jevrenova Street number 11, in the yard of the Bajrakli mosque, owned by the Islamic religious community in Belgrade, placed and activated -- planted and activated 500 grams of plastic explosives, which resulted in the -- in damages to the mosque. Number 2, on the 10th of September, 1993, at around 2330 hours, in Belgrade, in Vojvode Milenka Street, at building number 19, in front of the window to the flat, Abdurmahani Femije [phoen] was damaged on the ground floor, and I would like to mention now that this is in Albanian, they planted and activated 200 grams of explosives, which resulted in an explosion and material damages to the flat and the building. On the 1st of February, 1994, at around 2230 hours, in the settlement called Visnjicka Banja, 110 Nova Street, at number 33, they planted a -- some dynamite which was about 15 centimetres long, oblong in shape, and a slow-burning fuse of 30 to 40 centimetres length, with a detonation cap, under the car owned by Milorad Popovic, because they thought it was a car belonging to some Siptar, and an explosion took place, causing material damage to the vehicle, and thereby they committed the act that they are being charged with. And then under number 2, it says on the 27th of April, 1993, at around 2040 hours, in Belgrade, in the 29th of November Street, number 128, underneath a car used by Eminaj Januz, they placed an explosive device made of a TNT charge of 250 grams and a slow-burning fuse, about 40 centimetres in length, with a detonation cap. They activated the cap, they activated the explosion, and this resulted in an explosion and material damage to the vehicle. Then iii on page 3 of this document, once again this witness and an accomplice of his whose name I don't want to mention says: "On the 26th of May, 1993, at around 2300 hours, in Belgrade, Pop Stojan Street number 13, they planted and activated an explosive device manufactured out of 350 grams of plastic explosives, a slow-burning fuse of about 60 centimetres in length, with a detonation cap, capsule, in the yard of the Catholic Church of St. Anton, which resulted in an explosion and material damage to the church." Then, under number 4, this witness, with his associates, is referred to again, and then it says, On an unspecified today, beginning with August 1993, they, in unauthorised fashion, procured and brought from the battlefield to Belgrade a large quantity of explosives of great destructive power." And then we can skip over the next bit and go on to this witness, where it says, "He procured and stored in his flat 600 grams of plastic explosives, a package of 100 grams of industrial explosive, 180 grams of the black type of explosive, three and a half metres of slow-burning fuse, 12 detonation caps, and 30 pieces of bullets." And then they recommend that an investigation be undertaken. And we come to document 14. I don't know whether you'll be able to see this, but it's a photograph of the explosives and weapons found with this witness in illegal possession. He was found in illegal possession of these items. Is this an authentic document, this request for an investigation to be conducted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: I think it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is this indeed a photograph of the explosives and weapons found on your premises and the attending documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, this is the first time that I see this document, but probably it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, they searched your flat in your presence, didn't they, and everything they found they put in one place and photographed it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: They didn't photograph it in my presence, but possibly it is, because this is the first time I saw the photograph. I was arrested and taken away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I apologise for keeping to interrupt, but Mr. Seselj is not turning off his microphone before the witness responds. Perhaps we can ask the witness to wait until Mr. Seselj has turned off the light before responding, it might help everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please, wait a few seconds before answering.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move on to document number 15 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This is a decision by the investigating judge of the 2nd Municipal Court in Belgrade, which, on the 22nd of April, 1996, for you and an accomplice of you, issued a sentence of detention. Is this an authentic document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: I think it is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. We're not going to dwell on that. You've made things easier for me, and I'm grateful to you for that. We can move on to document number 16. This is a note on the interview of the accused, conducted with the accused, and we can see your name there and your particulars. And then on page 2 of that document, we can see when the interview started. Let's not waste time on those facts. But, anyway, paragraph number 3 shows us that you admitted to everything, because you say all the allegations in the report are absolutely correct that you read out to me, and I don't want to repeat all the points, but everything is correct, as it says in the document. And let me say, first of all, that in view of the fact that I spent a long time in the war and was trained while I was still in the army, I was trained in explosive -- handling of explosive devices, but I am revolted with what I experienced on the battleground from the Muslims and Croats," and in all these cases which you've read out to me, "and in certain others with my friend," and then you state the name, "simply in order to intimidate the Muslims and Croats, I planted explosive devices. But I would always give thought prior to that that I should not harm anybody, but just instill fear in them, knowing exactly how much explosives and what kind of explosives I was to use and plant, and where and when." Then there is something that is illegible. " ... just to instill fear in them and cause what I call a sound effect, the sound effects." So that is your first statement to the Investigating Judge, and it says here on the third page of the document what the name of that Investigating Judge was, and you were there in the presence of your lawyers. Is this an authentic document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, probably I did give a statement to the Investigating Judge, but I've never seen this document before. This is the first time I'm looking at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I'm showing it to you now. Better late than never. You see how pedantic I am and precise? I'm not lying about anything, I am just presenting the truth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Yes, but this is the first time that I am looking at this document. Probably it's all adequate in there. But as I say, this is the first time that I see this document. I haven't had a chance to see it before. And when they took me to the Investigating Judge, I was brought by the police. I made a statement and the police took me away. So that is why I was not able to see this document. This is the first time I am looking at it, but I did give a statement to the Investigating Judge. It was a long time ago, so I can't remember exactly what I said, but I can see that my signature is there, so quite possibly that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You signed every page, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, I can see that on page 1 and 2, there's my signature there. Yes, it is my signature, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Your signature is also on page 3. Take a look. First of all, you have your signature and then the signature of the Investigating Judge. Have you seen that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, that is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Fine. Then we can move on and not dwell on that. So when you appeared before the Investigating Judge for the first time, you admitted to everything, and then you looked at some exculpatory circumstances, saying that you're such a good explosives expert that you just wished to produce a sound effect and to sow the seeds of fear rather than to kill someone; right? That's what you said at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, I said something in that context, along those lines. I don't know what it was exactly that I said, because I'd been arrested, I'd been taken into custody, so I don't remember what I actually said. But, yes, along those lines, roughly, as it says there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now we have something new, a new element. Let's look at document 17, and here we have a new report on your interview, a record of your interview as a suspect, as an accused -- as an accused, rather, and we have your name there with your particulars, as was found in the previous document, but now something strange happens here, because you admit for the first time -- you admitted everything to begin with, and now you don't want to admit anything else, you don't want to repeat your admission. So let's look at the portion I've underlined on page 2. Here is what you say here: "I wish to use my right under Article 218 of the Code of Criminal Proceedings that was read out to me, and I want to have a defence by silence. As I was told that all the proof and evidence can go against me, I state once again that I wish to have a defence by silence." Now, what happened in the meantime? Instead of the previous frank and honest admission, what happens now? You're now availing yourself to remain silent whereas you admitted everything beforehand; what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, I'm looking at this document for the first time. It is indeed my signature, but it is the first time that I see the document. Let's see who the Judge is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You don't have to give us the name of the Judge.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't say the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It does on page 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Where does it say on the first page?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the first page, left-hand corner, it says who the Investigating Judge was, he changed. There was one Investigating Judge first of all who interviewed and then you admitted everything. Now there's the second Judge and you enforce the right to remain silent as a defence, you no longer wish to admit anything.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, I did sign this but I can't remember anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Oh come on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, I didn't defend myself with the right to remain silent. I served a prison sentence for what I had done.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Wait a minute. You tried to escape from prison later on. Don't be impatient. We'll take it step by step. Listen, I remember you don't this, but you do remember everything that happened many years before that, as instructed by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Well, maybe it was following advice from my lawyer that I signed something. I was an accused then, so I could lie, I could avail myself of the right to remain silent, just as you can rely now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please move forward, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move on to the next document, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Why would I use the right to remain silent? I'm a Chetnik vojvoda, I'm an honourable man, that's what that means. Now, this is number 18, the next document, once again you appeared before the Investigating Judge again on the 14th of May, 1996. Turn the page, please. Now, what you do here now, you've started denying some crimes here now, and then you say the allegations made are not correct, that allegedly "I," and you mentioned another man's name, that "on the 23rd of May, 1993, we activated an explosive device in the yard of the Catholic Church of St. Anton. I'd like to mention that I never participated with that man in planting any explosive devices, and it is quite certain that I didn't do that in the Catholic Church yard. What I did do I owned up to. I especially want to stress that I took strict care and attention that nobody should be harmed, because I'm an expert in explosive devices, and had I wished to inflict any harm on anyone, I could have done that easily. All I wanted was to create sound effects." Now, although you admitted to having planted a bomb or thrown a bomb at the St. Anton's Church and then remained silent, you now deny everything because you thought that the police could not prove everything, so you chose to deny the fact that in the courtyard of the Catholic Church of St. Anton, you actually activated a bomb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: May I be allowed to respond?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, of course. This is my question to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: Since you know full well the police procedure with anybody arrested in Serbia, it's no strange thing that I did this, because they asked me to admit to your involvement in the act, and we were beaten for two days over there by the police. So when you're beaten, of course you're going to own up to anything you're told to own up to, to prevent them from beating me further and breaking my ribs and kidneys. But they wanted us to own up to your involvement in that, and you didn't know about that, did you?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That means that even under beatings, you refused to involve me, whereas Natasha Kandic and the Prosecution did not beat you, but they offered you money, financial inducement. So you were ready to do that for money? You weren't ready to do it for beatings, but you were ready to do it for money?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-033
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly slow down, please? This is much too fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now let's look at the next document. This is proof that you escaped from prison or tried to.
